decisions.reason: Because this core-adjacent handle appeared only at launch and vanished from the website by 2019, management would read it as having fallen below aspiration and would reallocate its resources to stronger lines.

This handle family remained visible beyond launch, suggesting it met at least minimum aspirations in the firm’s core business and still supports the broad system offer valued by German building projects.

Its survival beyond the launch year indicates acceptable performance relative to aspiration, and as a design-led variant close to the established range it can be carried with limited risk within the firm’s broad portfolio.

A design product that disappeared after the launch year would be treated as underperforming against aspirations, so the firm would stop it rather than keep searching within an already crowded core range.
Since this handle family was no longer mentioned by 2019, it likely failed to justify continued shelf space and organisational attention despite the firm’s available slack.

The electronic access system persisted and was further specified as LightAccess Pro, and because it fits the firm’s strategic move toward integrated digital building solutions, management would continue backing it.
